te.title: Vacuum unit upset
te.sit: The vacuum unit had a pump problem. Your heater is firing much harder.

te.title: Water in the naphtha
te.sit: The debutanizer reports free water in the feed. LIC-101 is higher than usual.

te.title: Products overlapping, tower ΔP low
te.sit: After last week's upset the gaps between products have closed by a few degrees: naphtha end point up, diesel 5 % point down, AGO 10 % point down. The tower ΔP is well below normal.

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Reflux climbing, nothing obvious (Atmospheric Crude Unit)
meta.sit: Night shift says FIC-101 has crept up all night while TIC-102 held. Fuel gas is a little higher too.

0.1.unit: The atmospheric crude unit takes 218.75 m³/h (190 t/h) of light crude through the cold preheat (E-1, E-3, E-2, E-14), the desalters V-3 // S-1, the hot preheat (E-15, E-4 on the mid pumparound, E-5 and E-7 on the bottom pumparound, E-6, E-8 // E-18) to 276 °C, the fired heater H-1 (two passes, 388 °C) and the 30-tray tower V-1. It makes naphtha (top, reflux drum V-4), diesel (tray 20, stripper V-2A), AGO (tray 12, stripper V-2B) and atmospheric residue to the vacuum unit. TIC-102 holds the top at 136.1 °C by resetting the reflux FIC-101; the pumparounds MPA (FIC-104, 87.5 m³/h through E-4) and BPA (FIC-108) remove heat lower in the tower and give it to the crude.

rows.what: Reflux FIC-101 crept up from 89.5 to 102.7 m³/h (+15 %) and was still climbing

0.4.ctx: Night shift, design rate, same crude tank all night; no maintenance or operating change reported; weather normal. Normal: reflux ≈ 89.5 m³/h, fuel gas ≈ 547 Nm³/h, MPA 87.5 m³/h returning at ≈ 210 °C.

R.1.p: The tower is an energy balance: the heat the feed brings in above the flash zone must leave through the pumparounds (MPA, BPA) and the top (condensed reflux). TIC-102 holds the top temperature, so whatever the pumparounds do not remove, the reflux must: FIC-101 is the balancing item. The pumparound heat goes into the crude, so less pumparound duty also means colder crude at the heater and more fuel at the same coil outlet.

R.2.eq: Q = ṁ · cp · ΔT for each side of an exchanger;  Q = U · A · ΔT_lm (the exchanger itself);  tower: Q_feed = Q_top + Q_MPA + Q_BPA + Q_products

TOP: more reflux needed to hold the top at the same feed
 OR — more heat reaches the top

evidence.text: FIC-101 reflux rose from 89.5 to 102.7 m³/h (+15 %) between 00:01:00 and 00:30:00 as a slow drift; the climb was still going at 00:30.
TIC-102 tower top stayed on its set point 136.1 °C within 3 °C (137.2 °C at 00:30:00).
FIC-106 fuel gas rose from 548 to 635 Nm³/h (+16 %) while TIC-101 held 388.0 °C.
First alarm: TI-184 LO Crude out of E-4 at 0:06:34; then TI-185 LO Crude out of E-5 at 0:10:18. No other alarm.
FIC-104 mid pumparound flow steady at 87.4 m³/h (SP 87.5), its output steady at 58.4 %.
TI-1014 (MPA return after E-4) rose from 210.2 to 248.7 °C while TI-1013 (MPA draw) rose only 277.0 → 283.9 °C: the MPA cooling across E-4 fell from 66.7 to 35.2 °C.
TI-184 (crude out of E-4) fell from 188.5 to 177.1 °C; TI-185 (crude out of E-5) fell from 202.1 to 191.9 °C.
MPA duty (DCS calculation) fell from 3654 to 1936 kW (-47 %); BPA duty rose from 4186 to 4559 kW (+9 %).
TI-1003 heater inlet fell from 276.2 to 272.7 °C; TIC-101 on its set point 388.0 °C; flash zone TI-1018 371.1 °C.
TI-1015 reflux temperature 46.2 → 48.3 °C (+2.2): a small rise that followed the reflux climb, not before it.
FIC-100 naphtha 47.5 → 46.5 m³/h and naphtha end point AI-101 204.1 → 202.4 °C: no more light material reaches the top; TI-170 crude from storage on design (53.3 °C).
PI-114 tower top 48.5 → 54.0 kPa g; tower ΔP 27.5 → 29.2 kPa, far below the 45 kPa flooding alarm.
Field (Visual plant, 0:30:00): local reflux gauge FG-101 102.4 m³/h against FIC-101 102.7 m³/h on the board: they agree.
Field (0:33:00–0:34:30): P-9A running, P-9B stopped (standby); FIC-104 87.7 m³/h at the pump; HV-961 (E-4 MPA inlet block valve) open; at E-4 TI-1014 248.3 °C, TI-184 177.0 °C.
Heat balance on E-4: the MPA gives 1718 kW less; the crude receives ≈ 1498 kW less (190 t/h × 2.49 kJ/(kg·K) × 11.4 K). Two independent instrument sets agree within 13 %.
T-2 MPA flow step (0:38:30): FIC-104 87.5 → 104.7 m³/h (+20 %) raised the MPA duty only 1929 → 2143 kW (+11 %); FIC-101 103.5 → 103.2 m³/h (no change) in 10 min; TI-1014 stayed at 249.6 °C.

hyp.cause: E-4 transfers less heat (fouled bundle, MPA or crude side)
hyp.ifthen: If E-4 transfers less heat, the MPA leaves E-4 hotter and the crude colder at the same FIC-104 flow; the tower must reject that heat at the top (more reflux) and the heater must make up the lost preheat (more fuel).
hyp.key: TI-1014 ↑, TI-184 ↓, MPA ΔT ↓ at FIC-104 steady; FIC-101 ↑, FIC-106 ↑
hyp.fals: MPA ΔT across E-4 unchanged; or the two sides of E-4 disagree in the heat balance

hyp.cause: FT-101 reflux meter drifting high (no real change)
hyp.ifthen: If only FT-101 drifts, the real reflux is unchanged and nothing else in the tower or the preheat moves.
hyp.key: FG-101 (local) below FIC-101; no change in the MPA, preheat or fuel
hyp.fals: FG-101 agrees with FIC-101; other variables move

hyp.cause: Overhead cooling weak (warmer reflux needs more flow)
hyp.ifthen: If E-9 / E-10 cool less, the reflux comes back warmer first, and more of it is needed to hold the top.
hyp.key: TI-1015 and TI-1016 rise several °C before FIC-101 climbs
hyp.fals: TI-1015 rises little and only after the reflux climb

hyp.cause: MPA flow really lower than FIC-104 shows (P-9A worn or FT-104 reading high)
hyp.ifthen: If less MPA really flows, the MPA is cooled further across E-4 (larger ΔT) and the pump sounds or reads off.
hyp.key: MPA ΔT across E-4 ↑; P-9A noisy or low local flow
hyp.fals: MPA ΔT ↓; P-9A normal; local flow = DCS

hyp.cause: Lighter crude after a tank change (more light ends to the top)
hyp.ifthen: If the crude is lighter, more naphtha reaches the top: FIC-100 rises and the light-end analyses fall.
hyp.fals: FIC-100 steady or falling; no tank change

hyp.cause: More heat into the tower from H-1 (coil outlet higher than shown)
hyp.ifthen: If H-1 sends more heat, the flash zone runs hotter and more vapour goes up; the heater inlet does not change.
hyp.fals: TI-1003 falls (the heater makes up lost preheat); flash zone on design

hyp.cause: MPA under-circulated for today’s heat load (FIC-104 set point too low)
hyp.ifthen: If the MPA flow is simply too low, raising FIC-104 restores the pumparound duty and the reflux falls back.
hyp.key: After +20 % on FIC-104: MPA duty ↑ ≈ 20 %, FIC-101 ↓ several m³/h
hyp.fals: MPA duty rises little and FIC-101 does not move

hyp.cause: E-4 MPA line-up wrong (HV-961 left partly closed)
hyp.ifthen: If HV-961 throttles the MPA, FCV-104 must open further to hold the flow, and the field finds the valve partly shut.
hyp.key: FIC-104 OUT ↑; HV-961 not fully open
